subject: physics
title: Mechanics Adventure 3: Work, energy and power
welcome_lead: Today you'll calculate work done and harness power.
meta_desc: Physics — work W=Fd cosθ, kinetic energy ½mv², potential energy mgh, power P=Fv.
final_note: You learned W = Fd cosθ, KE = ½mv², PE = mgh, energy is conserved, and P = W/t = Fv.

concepts.def: Total E constant in isolated system

walkthroughs.body_html:
W = F · d · cosθ, where θ is angle between F and d.

If F ⊥ d → cosθ = 0 → no work (e.g. circular motion).
If F same direction as d → W = Fd.

Negative work: F opposite to motion (friction).

Kinetic: KE = ½mv².
Gravitational PE: PE = mgh.
Elastic PE in spring: ½kx².

Energy conservation: total E in isolated system is constant.

Roller coaster: PE → KE → PE → KE, total constant (ignoring friction).

Power = rate of energy transfer:

P = W/t = Fv

1 W = 1 J/s. Human cyclist ~250 W; car engine ~50-100 kW; nuclear plant ~1 GW.

Efficiency = useful output / total input × 100%.
Car ~25%. Coal plant ~35%. LED ~90%.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.
Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.

mcqs.q: What property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
options: The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
The frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
Amplitude determines pitch — a bigger wave is a higher-pitched note.

mcqs.q: In which direction does an electric field point near a positive charge?
options: Radially outwards — the field is defined by the force on a positive test charge, which is repelled.
There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
Radially inwards because positive attracts negative.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
